newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanians rescued off Italy in nighttime drama.
newsitem.headline: Albanians rescued off Italy in nighttime drama.

text.p: More than 800 Albanian refugees were rescued in a dramatic overnight operation on Sunday after the small navy ship they were crammed on ran aground off the Italian port of Brindisi.
Coastguards, battling against heavy seas and bitterly cold winds, spent seven hours evacuating the 858 men, women and children from the rusty Albanian patrol boat.
The deck of the F324 naval vessel was heaving with people while some men perched on top of the commuications mast, waving a white rag at a flotilla of rescue ships.
"We travelled with our hearts in our mouths," said 19-year old student Kulluri Bardhxl after he had been pulled to safety. "It was the most terrifying experience of my life."
The refugees included a woman who was about to give birth, a 10-day old baby and dozens of tiny children -- pale and exhausted after their ordeal across the Adriatic sea.
Coastal authorities said the 858, plus 317 others who arrived on three fishing boats in the port of Bari further north, took the total of arrivals overnight to 1,175.
"Working in that sea to save all those people, and in the shallows, and without anyone being injured was exceptional," said Brindisi port commander Giovanni Biso.
"They were piled one on top of each other, on a boat no longer than 50 metres, and this increased the risks of the rescue," he told reporters.
"Fortunately now the seas are picking up and we hope that maybe that will be enough to halt the exodus."
The port is a centre for evacuations of foreigners from Albania as well as being a magnet for refugees fleeing the anarchy that has swept the impoverished Balkan state.
Italy, which evacuated around 1,000 people from Albania earlier in the week, sent helicopters to Tirana on Sunday to bring out another 30 people trapped in the capital.
The Foreign Ministry in Rome said they were nine Italians, two Algerians, four Brazilians and 15 Albanians.
The United States has also been flying its citizens and other foreigners into Brindisi from Tirana.

The Albanians on the patrol boat said they left home mid-morning on Saturday after commandeering the small patrol boat in the southern port of Vlore, which has been an epicentre of unrest with mobs in orgies of looting and shooting.
They first tried to dock further south at Otranto and then Lecce on the heel of Italy, but were turned away.

The authorities finally gave them permission to dock at Brindisi when their engine started to fail, but just before midnight as they were being escorted ashore, the boat drifted into shallows some 400 metres from a petro-chemical plant.
Helicopters circled overhead, their searchlights sweeping the black seas to make sure no-one fell overboard.

The rescue ships kept their distance to prevent the desperate Albanians from trying to swim out to them, while small flat-bottomed speed boats, bobbing wildly in the swell, picked up the refugees in groups of about 30.

"I want to come to Italy because there are discos here. We don't have any in my village," said Gentian Belloj, a young conscript who had deserted from the Albanian army the week before. "We don't have any food, money or work back home."

The refugees only brought the clothes they stood in. When they were dropped off at the dockside, cordons of police escorted them away to be finger-printed and then bused them out to temporary shelters. The final group came ashore after dawn.
The refugees, mostly young men, said they had had a horrifying 12-hour voyage to Brindisi across the narrow stretch of water that divides Italy from Albania.
"We all tried to pilot the boat, but it was complete anarchy with the strongest people taking command," said Bardhxl.
